brief: Hungary's payments infrastructure layer is unusually well documented for a normally opaque niche, because its two core operators are subject to Hungarian 'üvegzseb' transparency: GIRO Zrt. (BKR, GIROInstant/AFR, qvik) publishes a dated supplier-contract register naming its IT vendors, and KELER/KELER KSZF publish a contract-disclosure section — together the highest-value primary sources in this cell. Around them sit the MNB as owner-and-overseer (payment infrastructure pages, annual Fizetési rendszer jelentés, qvik participant hub), which supplies the authoritative actor map and forward mandate signals such as AFR 2.0. The card layer is split between scheme certification regimes that function as supplier directories — Visa's Global Registry of Service Providers is openly searchable, while Mastercard's GVCP certified-vendor listing is behind Mastercard Connect — and a concentrated personalisation/processing hub set: ANY Biztonsági Nyomda (BÉT-listed, works with Thales DIS), CARDNET, Euronet, with Worldline and Nexi Central Europe pressing in from the region. The main blind spot is that no public source attributes the GIROInstant core platform to a named technology vendor; that fact must be triangulated from the contract register, recruitment adverts and MNB documentation.
